title: Calculations using simple and compound interest

sections.title: Calculations using simple and compound interest

subtopics.title: Hire purchase repayments
subtopics.exposition: A hire purchase agreement is a financial agreement between the shop and the customer about how the customer will pay for the desired product. The principal amount of a hire purchase loan is the cash price minus the deposit. The interest on a hire purchase loan is always charged at a simple interest rate and only on the amount owing. Most hire purchase agreements require a deposit to be paid before the customer can take the product. The simple interest formula used for hire purchase is A = P(1 + in). The accumulated loan is worked out using the number of years the loan is needed for. The total (accumulated) loan amount is divided into monthly payments over the period of the loan. When a deposit is paid as a percentage of the cash price, first find the deposit as that percentage of the cash price (10% of R2500 = 250). The principal P is the cash price minus the deposit (2500 - 250 = 2250), a new opening balance because the deposit is paid in cash. Substitute P, i and n into A = P(1 + in) to find the accumulated loan amount (A = 2250(1 + 0.075 x 2) = 2587.50). The monthly repayment is the accumulated loan amount divided by the number of monthly payments (2587.50 / 24 = 107.81). The monthly payment is also called the monthly instalment. The interest rate is written as a decimal in the formula (7.5 % p.a. is i = 0.075). The number of years n is the number of months divided by 12 (24 months gives n = 24/12 = 2). If a hire purchase question does not mention a deposit, assume no deposit was paid, so the principal is the cash price.

subtopics.title: Hire purchase with insurance premium
subtopics.exposition: The insurance premium is an amount of money paid monthly that gives the customer more time between a missed payment and possible repossession of the product. A shop can add a monthly insurance premium to the monthly instalments of a hire purchase agreement. Write down the known variables: with no deposit P is the cash price (5500), i is the rate as a decimal (0.21) and n is the months divided by 12 (54/12 = 4.5). Use the simple interest formula to find the accumulated loan (A = 5500(1 + 0.21 x 4.5) = 10 697.50). Divide the accumulated loan by the number of monthly payments to get the monthly instalment before insurance (10 697.50 / 54 = 198.10). Add the monthly insurance premium to the monthly instalment to get the monthly payment (198.10 + 12.50 = 210.60).

subtopics.title: Inflation and prices
subtopics.exposition: Inflation is the average increase in the price of goods each year and is given as a percentage. Inflation is calculated using the compound interest formula, since the rate of inflation increases year on year. The compound interest formula used for inflation is A = P(1 + i)^n. To find a future cost, take the current price as P, the inflation rate as a decimal i (9 % is 0.09) and the number of years as n. Substitute into A = P(1 + i)^n to get the future price (A = 14(1 + 0.09)^4 = 19.76). To find a past cost, take today's price as A, the inflation rate as a decimal i (11 % is 0.11) and the number of years as n; the past price is the unknown P. Substitute the known values into A = P(1 + i)^n and solve for P (55 = P(1 + 0.11)^3). Solve for P by dividing A by (1 + i)^n (P = 55 / (1 + 0.11)^3 = 40.22).

subtopics.title: Population growth
subtopics.exposition: Family trees increase exponentially because every person born has the ability to start another family. Population growth is calculated using the compound interest formula. The expected population after n years is found with the compound interest formula A = P(1 + i)^n. Take the current population as P, the annual growth rate as a decimal i (2.1 % is 0.021) and the number of years as n. Substitute into A = P(1 + i)^n to get the expected population (A = 3 888 180(1 + 0.021)^10 = 4 786 343).
